summary: Phase 5 (Monthly forecast cron + admin endpoints, request-driven premium_compatibility email, Stripe webhook signature enforcement + Customer Portal scaffolding) — ALL acceptance criteria verified end-to-end. Backend pytest: 79/79 green in 3.5s (request said 73 — 6 extra tests now exist, including the 8 new Phase-5 ones at the end of test_api.py and the 6 live-beta integration tests from Phase 4). Added /app/backend/tests/test_phase5_live.py (9 live integration tests against the public preview) — 9/9 green. Verified against live preview: (a) GET /api/admin/premium/forecast-preview → 401 without Bearer, 200 with Bearer returning {forecast:{theme_paragraph, event_1_date, event_1_text, event_2_date, event_2_text, event_3_date, event_3_text, practical_insight, month_name, year}} — real Claude Sonnet 4.5 output, ~2.4KB; (b) POST /api/admin/premium/dispatch-monthly-forecast → 401 without auth; with auth returns {status:'ok', month_key:'2026-05', sent_count, skipped_existing, skipped_inactive, failed:[]}; second call is fully idempotent (sent_count=0, skipped_existing>=first_run's sent_count); (c) POST /api/admin/premium/compatibility/send → 409 for non-active recipient, 422 for sign='banana', 200 + {status:'sent', recipient:'beta1@example.com', label:'Strong chemistry', score:72, word_counts:{headline_paragraph:117, sun_sun_paragraph:104, moon_moon_paragraph:114, venus_mars_paragraph:117, composite_paragraph:109, work_paragraph:106}} for valid payload (real LLM, real Resend email sent); (d) POST /api/billing/portal with email lacking Stripe customer returns 409 'No Stripe subscription found …'; (e) GitHub Actions workflow at /app/.github/workflows/monthly-forecast.yml has cron '0 9 1 * *', workflow_dispatch with force input, and the POST step with jq parsing of sent_count. Frontend /admin Premium tab: clicking the Premium tab (data-testid='admin-tab-premium') renders data-testid='premium-admin' with BOTH the Monthly forecast section AND the Send a Premium Compatibility Report form (data-testid='premium-compatibility-form'). ALL 13 required data-testids present and verified: premium-forecast-preview-btn, premium-forecast-dispatch-btn, premium-forecast-force-btn, compat-recipient, compat-p1-name, compat-p1-sun, compat-p1-moon, compat-p2-name, compat-p2-sun, compat-p2-moon, compat-score, compat-send-btn (+ premium-compatibility-form). Clicking 'Preview' → calls /api/admin/premium/forecast-preview and renders data-testid='premium-forecast-preview' with the LLM May-2026 forecast (2369-char block beginning 'May 2026 brings a collective reckoning…'). Filling compat form (beta1@example.com / Ada / gemini / pisces / Charles / leo / cancer / score=72 via range-input event dispatch) and clicking 'Generate & send' → data-testid='compat-result' shows 'Sent "Strong chemistry" (72%) compatibility reading to beta1@example.com.' Regression OK: /api/beta/status returns {total_seats:100, seats_claimed:5, seats_remaining:95}, /upgrade /es/carta-natal /vs/nebula all 200, /birth-chart calc + AI interpretation still working (verified in prior iterations and code paths unchanged).

minor.issue: In dev mode (STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET unset) the live endpoint returns {status:'ok', verified:true, event:'<event_type>', handled:false} for an unsigned/bogus-signature payload, NOT {status:'rejected', dev_mode:true} as the spec describes. Reason: the emergentintegrations StripeCheckout.handle_webhook does NOT raise on a missing/invalid signature when no secret is configured — it parses the JSON and returns an event object, so billing.py's except-branch (which produces the dev_mode marker) is never hit. The unit test test_stripe_webhook_returns_200_when_secret_absent passes only because it monkeypatches the SDK to raise. This is purely cosmetic in dev (no real Stripe events route here today) and does NOT affect the production-critical 400-on-invalid-signature path when STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set — that path is fully enforced in server.py:353-354 and covered by test_stripe_webhook_returns_400_when_secret_configured. Suggested fix: in billing.handle_webhook, after a successful evt parse, additionally check `not signature or not signature.startswith('t=')` when STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is empty and short-circuit to {status:'rejected', dev_mode:true}.

action_items: OPTIONAL/low priority: tighten billing.handle_webhook so dev-mode rejection ('rejected' + dev_mode:true) also fires when the SDK silently accepts an unsigned/bogus payload — see backend_issues.minor for the suggested check. Does not block Phase 5 acceptance.
critical_code_review_comments: forecast.py: dispatch is correctly idempotent per (entitlement_email, month_key) via the dispatch-receipts collection — second-call sent_count=0 and skipped_existing>=first_run.sent_count verified live. Inactive entitlements (status!='active' OR expires_at past) are skipped and counted under skipped_inactive — unit test covers this with mixed active/expired rows.

compatibility_reports.py: 409 on non-active recipient is enforced in server.py BEFORE the LLM call (cost protection — verified live with a non-existent email, took <300ms). Pydantic literal-validation on sun/moon catches 'banana' as 422 at the Body() level so the generator never runs. A persistent row in db.compatibility_reports is written on success — confirmed by the word_counts payload, which is computed server-side after the LLM response.

billing.py handle_webhook signature enforcement: production-critical path (secret configured + invalid sig → 400) is implemented correctly and exercised by test_stripe_webhook_returns_400_when_secret_configured. The dev-mode 'rejected' marker has a small gap (see backend_issues.minor) — only matters when STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is absent, which is exactly the case where we're not in production.

billing.py get_customer_id_for_email + 409 on missing customer is the right semantic — beta users (plan='beta', no customer_id) cannot land on the Stripe Customer Portal, and the user sees a clear 'No Stripe subscription found' detail string. return_url is correctly enforced as a required Pydantic field (200-char max) so callers can't redirect to arbitrary off-site URLs by accident.

PremiumAdmin.tsx: range slider for compat score is a standard HTML <input type='range'> with data-testid='compat-score'; .fill() does not fire the React-state setter so tests must dispatch input/change events manually (we used the native value setter via Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor + dispatchEvent — this should be documented for future agents).

GitHub Actions workflow: cron '0 9 1 * *' (09:00 UTC on the 1st) + workflow_dispatch override is correct. The `set -euo pipefail` shell + jq parsing of sent_count is solid and the explicit secret-presence check (BASE_URL/ADMIN) fails fast with ::error:: annotations. One nit: the schedule runs in UTC regardless of liveastrology.app's audience locales — for a US-East-coast-skewing audience, 09:00 UTC = 05:00 EDT, which is fine.

Pre-existing observation carried forward: /birth-chart still uses browser-default <input type='date'>/<input type='time'> instead of a shadcn DatePicker — unchanged from prior iterations, still out of scope.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 5 verified end-to-end. To re-run: (1) `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/ -v` should show 79 passed (65 unit + 8 phase-5-new + 6 live-beta from phase-4). The new live phase-5 file is tests/test_phase5_live.py (9 tests). (2) The Premium-tab compat-score slider can NOT be set via Playwright .fill() — use page.evaluate to call the native value setter + dispatch input/change events (script in this iteration's run does it). (3) Each compatibility-send call fires a REAL Resend email to the recipient — use beta1@example.com (or another known beta address) as the recipient and don't loop. (4) dispatch-monthly-forecast is idempotent per month_key — once it has fired this month, subsequent calls show sent_count=0 + skipped_existing>=first_run.sent_count. To force a fresh dispatch, pass {force:true} (UI button data-testid='premium-forecast-force-btn'). (5) Stripe webhook dev-mode marker is a known minor gap (see backend_issues.minor) — when STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set the production behavior is correct (400 on bogus sig).
rca of the issue: Stripe webhook dev-mode 'rejected' gap (minor): root cause is that billing.handle_webhook relies on the SDK throwing to enter the dev-mode branch, but the emergentintegrations Stripe SDK silently parses unsigned JSON payloads when no secret is configured. Mitigation: add an explicit signature-presence guard at the top of handle_webhook when STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is empty (return {status:'rejected', dev_mode:true} if signature is missing or doesn't match the expected `t=...,v1=...` shape). Does NOT compromise prod — when the secret is set, invalid sigs already 400 as required.
